short: The colossal chryselephantine Statue of Zeus at Olympia, created by Phidias, was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
full:
Sculpted by the renowned artist Phidias around 435 BCE, the Statue of Zeus was the centrepiece of the Temple of Zeus in the sanctuary of Olympia. Standing nearly 13 metres tall, the seated figure of the king of the gods was constructed from ivory plates and gold panels over a wooden framework, holding a figure of Nike (Victory) in his right hand.

The statue was universally admired in antiquity for its majestic and awe-inspiring presence, with the Roman general Aemilius Paulus reportedly moved to tears upon seeing it. It stood for over eight centuries before the temple was abandoned and the statue was either destroyed by fire in Olympia or carried off to Constantinople, where it eventually burned in the 5th century CE.
